note: Small Missouri River access at the end of 270th Street west of Langdon: a large open gravel lot at the boat ramp, with the primitive camping spot and a privy on its east edge against the trees, looking across the lot to the river. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: page 'Individual Campsites', Rule 140 standard; map (11/07) Primitive Camping Area symbol and privy on the east side of the ramp lot = GIS 369 = stored pin. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights now manual. Waterfront: riverfront -> riverview proposed (the open ground between the camping spot and the river is the boat-ramp parking lot). Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION: area page 'Things to Do When You Visit: Camping: Individual Campsites'; Rule 140 standard, no special-use-permit-only rule, no Rule 101; no brochure on the page. Map (11/07): a gravel loop road from 270th St. into a lot at the boat ramp, with the Primitive Camping Area symbol and a privy on the lot's east edge. GIS 27 point 369 'Primitive Camping Area' = stored pin; GIS 26 lot 24 (Paved) 27 m west. Imagery: a large open gravel lot (~60 x 90 m) reached by a gravel road, easily room for a 23-ft rig. A designated point at the lot, so it stays.

WATERFRONT (stored riverfront -> riverview, downgrade): the camping point is on the lot's east edge ~30-35 m from the Missouri River (~250 m wide, a river), and the ground between is open - but it is the boat-ramp parking lot and ramp approach, which is day use, not the campground's own apron (curation doc: no driveways or day use between; earlier MDC results: 'a ramp lot is not an open apron'). The river is plainly visible across the lot -> riverview. The stored evidence ('open gravel/sand lot running out to the Missouri River bank at the ramp') describes the same lot.
PIN: stored 40.33891,-95.62127 = GIS camping point 369, at the east edge of the lot; fine.
CLUSTERS: one camping point. near.py: Aspinwall Bend (13886) 2.5 km and Hoot Owl Bend Access (13836) 2.6 km are separate areas.
